title: Waymo Secures $5 Billion Loan to Accelerate Autonomous Ride-Hailing Expansion
key_facts: Waymo closed a $5 billion term loan on 8 Oct 2026, its first debt financing.
PIMCO, Blackstone and Sixth Street led the lender group; Goldman Sachs was sole lead bookrunner.
Waymo did not disclose the maturity or exact interest rate; 24/7 Wall St. says Alphabet's filings show no 8-K on the deal.
Bloomberg reported the loan was priced at 5.25 percentage points over the benchmark after starting at more than $3 billion.
Waymo's chief financial officer Steve Fieler called it 'an important step in our evolution into a scaling commercial enterprise'.
Waymo raised $16 billion in equity in February at a $126 billion valuation, majority-funded by Alphabet.
Waymo launched in its 15th US city in September.
quote_evidence: Even so, on October 8, 2026, its robotaxi unit Waymo closed a $5 billion term loan from private credit funds and institutional lenders.
It is Waymo’s first debt financing.
A syndicated term loan is a fixed sum put up by a group of lenders and repaid on a set schedule.
why_it_matters_hint: Waymo borrowing from outside lenders puts a market price on its risk and shows how much cash a driverless fleet needs.
notes: Chunk source Konsulteer is a copy site; read 24/7 Wall St. (analysis) and FintechNews CH (short report). Loan closed 8 Oct, reported 12 Oct.
